message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of solid, beginner‑friendly leg exercises you can add to your routine:

| Exercise | Primary Muscles Targeted | How to Do It (Basic Form) |
|----------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Squat** | Quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, core | Stand shoulder‑width apart, feet slightly angled out. Lower as if sitting back into a chair, keeping chest up and knees tracking over toes. Push through heels to return upright. |
| **Lunge (forward or reverse)** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Step forward (or backward) so both knees bend to ~90°. Keep torso upright, push off front foot to step back or switch legs. |
| **Deadlift (Romanian or conventional)** | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back | Hold barbell/weights at hip level, hinge at hips while keeping back neutral. Lower until you feel stretch in hamstrings, then pull back up using glutes and hamstrings. |
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Sit on machine, place feet hip‑width apart on platform. Push until legs almost straight but not locked; slowly lower back down. |
| **Calf Raise** | Calves (gastrocnemius & soleus) | Stand on a raised surface (step or block). Rise onto toes, pause, then lower heel below step level. |
| **Step‑Up** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Use a sturdy bench or box. Step one foot onto it, drive through heel to lift body, then step down and repeat on other side. |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Place rear foot on bench behind you. Lower front knee to ~90°, keep torso upright. Push through front heel to stand. |
| **Hip Thrust / Glute Bridge** | Glutes, hamstrings | Lie on floor/back against bench, feet flat on ground. Lift hips until shoulders to knees form a straight line. Squeeze glutes at top, lower slowly. |

### Quick Tips for All Leg Workouts

1. **Warm Up** – 5–10 min light cardio + dynamic stretches (leg swings, walking lunges).
2. **Progressive Overload** – Gradually increase weight or reps each week.
3. **Form First** – Prioritize proper technique over heavier loads to avoid injury.
4. **Recovery** – Allow 48 h between intense leg sessions; include foam rolling or gentle stretching afterward.

Feel free to mix and match these moves based on your goals—strength, hypertrophy, or endurance—and adjust sets/reps accordingly!
